subject: Cross-region data handoff authorization request — temporary analytical hop
content:
From: Laura Chen <laura@NimbusAnalytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-support@nimbusanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary analytic hop for APAC telemetry (authorization + roster)

Hi Jasmine,

Quick one — our analytics partner (third-party) needs to run a short processing job over a 48-hour maintenance window next month to rehydrate derived metrics for APAC users. They will spin up in our US cloud region to run the compute (no persistence beyond the job).

Questions from our security/compliance team:
- Do you allow transient processing outside APAC for customer data when the data remains encrypted at rest in APAC and the processing job accesses a minimal subset via a TLS channel?
- What subprocessors would be involved if Redwood routes the traffic through a US-based analytics edge for the job?
- Can Redwood provide a short DPA annex that covers transient hops, timeboxed use, and KMS key policy carve-outs for ephemeral compute?

We’ve attached our internal sign-off template — happy to share the job schedule once we know the constraints.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of IT Security, Nimbus Analytics

---
Attachment: job_request_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

-----Original Message End-----

----
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary analytic hop for APAC telemetry (authorization + roster)

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask, and good context. Short answers up-front: possible, with conditions.

We can support a timeboxed transient processing hop (APAC data temporarily accessed for a scheduled job in a non-APAC region) if all the following are accepted:
1) Customer explicitly approves the transient hop window (start/end timestamps).
2) Data in-flight and at-rest protections remain in place (TLS + at-rest encryption).
3) The processing job must not persist unencrypted data to any long-term storage in the non-APAC region; any derived dataset must be pulled back to APAC or deleted on job termination.
4) Subprocessors that will touch the data are disclosed and approved in advance.
5) We require a DPA annex and an ops playbook that captures rollback and audit steps for the window.

Action items from our side:
- Karthik: can you confirm the likely list of Redwood subprocessors (edge/egress) that would be implicated for a US-based ephemeral job and whether we can run the job under customer-managed KMS keys?
- Marissa: legal will need to draft a short annex for transient hops; can you estimate turnaround for a Nimbus-signed DocuSign?
- Markus: ops — what telemetry/audit logs can we guarantee for the 48h window (request/response traces, host artifacts, KMS key usage logs)?

Laura — once we have the roster, DPA annex, and a playbook, we can scope the authorization and provide a one-time temporary exception. Attaching Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3.pdf and our transient-egress-playbook.docx for your review.

Best,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3.pdf (DPA annex draft)
Attachment: transient-egress-playbook.docx (ops runbook stub)

-----Original Message End-----

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary analytic hop for APAC telemetry (authorization + roster)

Thanks for looping me in. Technical summary from infra:
- If the job is executed in a US region, the only Redwood-managed subprocessors likely to interact are our CDN/edge provider and our ephemeral compute orchestrator (both are already on the standard subprocessor roster; I’ll attach the current CSV).
- We can enforce customer-managed KMS for the job, but Nimbus must supply key access policies ahead of time (we’ll need the key ARNs and an access window).
- Audit coverage: we can provide request traces (per-token call traces), instance lifecycle events, and KMS key usage logs for the job window. Host-level forensic artifacts (core dumps) are considered sensitive and require a separate legal hold.

Operational constraints:
- Maximum concurrent workers we can allow under a transient exception: 25 nodes.
- Network egress must be restricted to the job’s target endpoints; ops will enforce egress firewall rules during the window.

I’m attaching subprocessor_roster_20271012.csv (current roster) and will flag the two subprocessors above as part of the approval package.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_20271012.csv (roster stub)

-----Original Message End-----

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@NimbusAnalytics.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary analytic hop for APAC telemetry (authorization + roster)

Hi Laura — copied Marissa from Legal.

We reviewed the draft annex and ops playbook. A few legal asks before we can sign off and issue the one-time exception: 
- Add explicit clause: "No long-term persistence outside APAC; all derived datasets must be validated and returned/deleted within the window."
- Add a narrow KMS key usage statement that limits key export and requires the customer-managed key be bound to the job run only.
- We need Nimbus to countersign the DocuSign for the DPA annex and accept the subprocessor roster for the one-time window.

Laura — I can prepare a redline. Expected turnaround: 48 hours once Nimbus confirms the precise 48h start/end timestamps and provides the key ARNs and contact for an on-call KMS admin.

If the above is accepted, ops (Karthik/Markus) will enable the transient window and we will capture the audit artifacts. Post-window we will send a short attestation confirming deletion of any transient artifacts.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
